schema: favorite synth/library -> what is loved -> targets (same target fields as genres.json)
checks: Every dna and v3_dna was parsed by core/dna.cpp parse() on main (library catalogue loaded) and by design/v3 canonical3() on preset-engine-2: no unknown NAME, no empty layer, at most 1024 bytes; stored in canonical form. Every recipe is design/v3 toRecipe(OneLine) and parses back (fromRecipe) to the same canonical DNA. K is computed from the measured root of the first key-tracked layer (windows-sounds.json, library note names), other tonal layers get T to the nearest octave. Nobody has listened to them yet.

favorites.name: Serum (Xfer Records)
favorites.loved_for: Visual wavetable editing and warp modes, clean (alias-free) oscillators, the drag-and-drop workflow, and the third-party preset economy around it. It defined the sound of 2010s EDM and future bass.
iconic: future-bass supersaw chords with pitch-bend wobble and sidechain pump
bright plucks for house and progressive
Third-party packs dominate; Splice lists its most popular Serum presets; Syntorial reports Serum as the second most-shared synth on Presetshare.

sources.title: Splice blog: 22 of the most popular Serum presets
Syntorial: best Serum presets (Serum second on Presetshare)

favorites.note: Factory preset names were not verified one by one; targets are by category.

favorites.name: Vital (Matt Tytel)
favorites.loved_for: Free, with the full engine; spectral warp modes; text-to-wavetable; a factory bank of 75 presets in the free tier; ultra-visual modulation.
iconic: clean modern basses and pads in the factory set

sources.title: MusicTech: Vital, a free wavetable synth with spectral warping

favorites.name: Pigments (Arturia)
favorites.kind: multi-engine synth (VA, wavetable, sample/granular, harmonic, modal)
favorites.loved_for: Colour-coded modulation, granular sample engine (from v2), additive harmonic engine (v3), sequencer-driven presets; reviewers call it a true power synth.

sources.title: Sound on Sound: Arturia Pigments 4 review

favorites.name: Diva (u-he)
favorites.kind: virtual analog with circuit-modelled filters and oscillators
favorites.loved_for: The filters and oscillators of classic polysynths and monosynths modelled at component level; "Divine" accuracy mode; reviewers single out the filters and the presets.

sources.title: Sound on Sound: u-he Diva review

favorites.name: Massive and Massive X (Native Instruments)
favorites.loved_for: Defined DnB and the dubstep explosion; wavetables like Carbon, Multiplex and Square-Saw were early-dubstep favourites; routing Osc 3 around the filter as the sub; performer LFO wobbles.

sources.title: Native Instruments blog: Massive, past presets and future (dubstep wavetables)

favorites.name: Sylenth1 (LennarDigital)
favorites.loved_for: Fat, CPU-light trance and EDM sound; its factory bank has been used everywhere; the go-to for trance leads, plucks and supersaw stacks.

sources.title: Loopmasters: the best Sylenth1 presets (factory bank "used and abused")

favorites.name: Spire (Reveal Sound)
favorites.loved_for: Big-room and trance leads, supersaws with many voices, efficient; a staple of EDM, trance and synthwave.

sources.title: Bedroom Producers Blog: Reveal Sound Spire review

favorites.name: Omnisphere (Spectrasonics)
favorites.loved_for: Huge psychoacoustic sample library (burned pianos, bowed and struck objects), deep layering, "Hardware Library" patches; used on hit records, games and film.
iconic: the ILIO Fame Series recreates famous sounds in it

sources.title: ILIO: The Fame Series, Classic Sounds for Omnisphere

favorites.name: Keyscape (Spectrasonics)
favorites.loved_for: Deeply sampled pianos and electromechanical keys, including rare ones (Clavinet-Pianet duo, Pianet T/N/M, CP-70, Wurlitzer 140B/200A, Rhodes Mark I, toy pianos).

favorites.name: Kontakt factory and famous libraries (Native Instruments and others)
favorites.loved_for: The platform for orchestral, cinematic and keyboard libraries: factory vintage organs, retro machines, orchestral; famous third-party: felt and upright pianos, scored strings, cinematic percussion, vocal-texture engines.

favorites.name: Arturia V Collection: Jupiter-8 V, Prophet V, Mini V, CS-80 V
favorites.loved_for: Faithful models of the classic polysynths and the Minimoog: Jupiter pads and arps, Prophet brass and sync, Minimoog bass and lead glide, CS-80 brass with expressive swells.
iconic: Jupiter-8 lush pads and sequenced arps

favorites.name: Nexus (reFX)
favorites.loved_for: Instant, mix-ready trance and EDM: trancegate pads (52 gate presets ship with it), supersaws, pianos and strings; expansions per genre.

favorites.name: Battery and the drum machines (808, 909, 707, LinnDrum, SP-1200, MPC)
favorites.loved_for: 808: the long boom kick, snappy snare, cowbell and claps; 909: punchy kick and sampled hats/cymbals; 707: bright, simple digital kit; LinnDrum: the 80s pop snare and claps; SP-1200: 12-bit 26.04 kHz grit; MPC: swing and pads. Battery has kits built around these machines.

sources.title: KVR forum: favorite 80s kits from Battery (606/707/808/909/DMX/LinnDrum kits)

favorites.name: LABS (Spitfire Audio)
favorites.loved_for: Free, simple, beautiful: Soft Piano (called the world's most popular piano plug-in by Spitfire), Strings, Frozen Strings (dry, textured; the spark for a paid library), Glass Piano, Trumpet Fields, Electric Piano, Drums.

sources.title: Rekkerd: Spitfire Audio launches LABS (Soft Piano, Strings)

favorites.name: Ableton Live factory instruments
favorites.kind: Operator, Wavetable, Drift, Simpler/Sampler, Collision, Tension, Electric, Drum Rack
favorites.loved_for: Operator FM (bells, basses; 20 years of presets curated by its designer), Wavetable, Drift (in every edition), Simpler slicing, physical models of mallets (Collision), strings (Tension) and e-piano (Electric); drum-machine core kits in Drum Racks.

sources.title: Sound on Sound: Ableton Live Drift synthesizer
